summary: Southern tip of White Head Island in the Grand Manan archipelago: station and diaphone fog alarm built 1929 after a 1927 residents' petition; combined building 1966.

light.fog_signal: diaphone, installed 1929 (LighthouseFriends); present signal: fog horn, blast 2 s, silence 18 s (CCG list); LighthouseFriends: two-second blast every twenty seconds when needed.
light.note: White rectangular tower with red top (Canadian Coast Guard list).

structures.type: square tower on a one-storey cement building
structures.note: Combined lighthouse and fog-alarm building; the square tower rises from one corner.
1929 fog-alarm house and dwelling; the whistle house was torn down shortly after 1966 and the old dwelling burned (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. Free 30-minute car ferry from Ingalls Head on Grand Manan; park on Long Point Road and walk about 1 km (or drive the last part by four-wheel-drive).

events.note: Petition from 330 residents of Grand Manan and Nova Scotia for a fog alarm at Long Point, sent to the Department of Marine in October 1927.
Contract for a fog-alarm building, dwelling and boathouse; agreement signed April 22, 1929; completion required by June 11.
Diaphone fog alarm driven by air compressed by two oil engines; three blasts of three seconds each minute.
Arthur Wilson the first keeper assigned to Long Point; served to 1958.
Combination lighthouse and fog-alarm building, one-storey cement with a square tower at one corner.
Whistle house torn down and the old keeper's dwelling burned, shortly after the 1966 building (LighthouseFriends gives no exact date).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'horn' matches the present Coast Guard fog signal (fog horn, blast 2 s, silence 18 s). LighthouseFriends' diaphone was the 1929 installation. No correction needed.

1929 is the station: LighthouseFriends dates the dwelling, fog-alarm building and first keeper to 1929. The 1966 date is the combined building that replaced them. LighthouseFriends does not give a separate date for the first lighting.

notes_for_editor: 1) Thin record. LighthouseFriends is the only source for the 1927-1966 history. The Canadian Coast Guard list gives the present light; the Department of Marine annual reports in the corpus (fiscal years to 1923-24) do not cover this station: 'Long Point' hits there are Ontario and Lake Erie stations, and 'Whitehead Island' hits are a Nova Scotia light. 2) Record's first_lit 1929 is not stated as a first lighting by LighthouseFriends; it is the station date and is treated as such. 3) Record's fog signal 'horn' was not a conflict: the CCG list (row 25, H4178) gives the present signal as a fog horn, blast 2 s, silence 18 s. The 1929 signal was the diaphone (LighthouseFriends). The earlier draft proposed a correction on the wrong premise; withdrawn. 4) CCG row read in full (2026-10-28): 'Long Point | Near S. extremity of Whitehead Island | Iso W 12s | focal height above water 15.6 m | nominal range 14 NM | White rectangular tower with red top | Fog Horn Blast 2 s; sil. 18 s'. The fields were checked against the row itself, not by column position alone. 5) Keepers after 1960 (Harvey, Morse, Tate) are named as LighthouseFriends lists them, with no personal detail. 6) Name hazards: Long Point, Ontario (Lake Erie) and other Long Point stations are different places; Long Eddy Point is on Grand Manan's North Head, not this station; Whitehead Island light (Canadian lists) is in Nova Scotia; the 1902 Gull Cove light was on this same island but is a separate station, discontinued 1981 per LighthouseFriends. 7) Contractor named in LighthouseFriends was omitted from the story. 8) Lorimer's 1876 pages 44-45 are read from the running heads in the archive.org text (p.44 header confirmed before the isthmus and herring passages; the p.45 header is missing from the OCR, so the herring passage is on 44 or 45). 9) Lorimer's timing: 'before low water and at the first of the flood' (corrected from an earlier 'at low water'). 10) LighthouseFriends' visitor note (grounds open, tower closed) was earlier recorded as unknown; corrected. 11) No newspaper or Canadian archival search was run for this station; the sources are thin and the story is kept short to match.
